resolution.rationale: Goals are still AIR-only upstream in v0.102.0: the upstream PR for a non-AIR opt-in (#1245) is still open, and no commit in v0.101.1..v0.102.0 adds a goal capability, so the patch is not absorbed. It replays onto v0.102.0 without conflict as c926f2b with the ledger's stable patch-id (650615ee, the same as ledger commit 72c0802), so its added, removed and context lines are unchanged. The v0.101.1..v0.102.0 edits of src/acp-agent.ts are the plans import and the three checklist call sites plus the conversation_reset plan removal (#1554), the workflow_progress field in the task_progress handler and the adoptTasks loop call (#1552, #1556), and a Fable 5.2 comment (#1557). None touches goalMeta, the GOAL_* constants, the initialize _meta builder (no AIR capability is added to or removed from the airSessionFailureCapabilityMeta list that the patch passes to goalMeta), the v1 _session/goal handler, publishGoal or publishRuntimeGoal. The /clear reset path that #1554 edits does not publish or clear the goal. src/goal-extension.ts, src/air-extension.ts, src/v2/initialize.ts and docs/air-extensions.md are unchanged upstream. @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.321 (#1557) still exports SDKActiveGoalMessage, and `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes on the candidate. The scoped run passes 14 tests (13 in acp-agent.test.ts, 1 in acp-v2.test.ts). The patch's src diff does not reverse-apply because later stacked patches rewrap the initialize _meta, so the core change was disabled in place: goalMeta's non-AIR branch returns meta unchanged. With it disabled, 'advertises and publishes goals for an opted-in non-AIR client' and 'advertises async tasks with steering and goals for an opted-in non-AIR client' fail. The pre-existing v2 follow-up is unchanged (see doubts).
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts src/tests/acp-v2.test.ts -t goal

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.102.0 still gates async tasks on the AIR asyncTasks capability only, so the provider-neutral opt-in is not absorbed. The patch replays onto v0.102.0 without conflict as c59a1a1 with the ledger's stable patch-id (1c6daa67, the same as ledger commit 374911d). src/async-tasks.ts, src/tool-calls/background.ts, src/v2/initialize.ts, README.md and docs/air-extensions.md are unchanged upstream, and so are stopsWorkflowsOnCancel and the backgroundedBashToolCall marker argument. Two upstream changes reach the code paths of an opted-in v1 client. #1552 adds the untyped workflow_progress snapshot in the task_progress handler, but passes it only to session.background.taskProgress (the v2 workflow card); the asyncTasks.taskProgress call that follows is byte-identical to v0.101.1 (task_id, description, summary, last_tool_name, usage, tool_use_id), so the async task lifecycle carries no workflow phases. #1556 adds SessionBackgroundWork.adoptTasks, called in the message loop before backgroundWork.sync, which returns [] unless the session's background list is reported. reported is backgroundWork.enabled && perTaskStopAffordance, and backgroundWork.enabled means a background sink, which only src/v2/agent.ts passes; v1AgentApp constructs ClaudeAcpAgent without one, so a v1 neutral client never gets an adopted task_<id> tool call. A throwaway probe in the candidate (inserted into acp-agent.test.ts, then reverted) ran one v1 scenario for an AIR asyncTasks client and for a neutral `_meta["async-tasks"]: true` client, both with `plan: {}`. The scenario has a Workflow tool call whose local_workflow task reports progress twice, the first time with a workflow_progress snapshot, and a second local_workflow task that no tool call started (the adoptTasks case). Both clients got identical async_task_spawned and async_task_progress updates, with no workflow phase text, no tool call with a task_ id, no state_update and no _claude/task item, and the neutral client got no jetbrains namespace. The same probe with the session's background forced to reported=true fails on an adopted 'task_hook1' tool call, so the probe does detect the v2 behaviour. #1554 touches only the checklist and plan removal next to asyncTasks.clear() in conversation_reset; asyncTasks.clear() itself is unchanged. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes. The scoped run passes 18 tests (8 in acp-agent.test.ts, 2 in acp-v2.test.ts, 7 in async-tasks.test.ts, 1 in create-session-options.test.ts). The patch's src diff does not reverse-apply because later stacked patches change the same initialize _meta and UNSERVED_EXTENSION_KEYS lines, so the core change was disabled in place. With clientSupportsAsyncTasks ignoring _meta['async-tasks'], seven tests fail: 'requires literal true for provider-neutral async task opt-in (true)', 'leaves workflows running for a provider-neutral client that opted into async tasks', 'stops one provider-neutral async task through the SDK without cancelling the prompt', 'publishes a Monitor task as a monitor to a provider-neutral async-task client', 'holds async_task_spawned until the Bash result brings the tool id for provider-neutral', 'keeps a provider-neutral async-task client's terminal running without the AIR marker' and 'advertises async tasks with steering and goals for an opted-in non-AIR client'. Removing 'async-tasks' from UNSERVED_EXTENSION_KEYS fails 'does not advertise the provider-neutral async tasks extension to a v2 client'. Passing asyncTasks.enabled again as the marker argument fails 'holds async_task_spawned until the Bash result brings the tool id for provider-neutral' and 'keeps a provider-neutral async-task client's terminal running without the AIR marker'.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts src/tests/acp-v2.test.ts src/tests/async-tasks.test.ts src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts -t "provider-neutral|neutral flag|async tasks|async-task|non-AIR"

resolution.rationale: settleAtResult is the Alas client-neutral form of the AIR backgroundSubagents capability, which upstream still offers to AIR only, so it is not absorbed. The patch replays onto v0.102.0 without conflict as ef35dff with the ledger's stable patch-id (656653e9, the same as ledger commit 1dcdf19). v0.102.0 does not change endsTurnsWithLiveSubagents, turnAwaitingSubagents, settleDeferredIfDrained, Turn.deferredSettle, the session_state_changed idle branch or the initialize advertisement, so the opt-in still goes through upstream's single gate, ACP v1 only. #1552 and #1556 change only the v2 background-work reporting (workflow card progress and adopted tool calls), which a settleAtResult client never gets because both features are v1 only on the patch side and v2 only upstream. The interaction checked was #1554: after the prompt is answered at its result, the follow-up cycles that subagent notifications start can write a checklist outside any turn. A throwaway probe (inserted into the 'with settleAtResult (Alas)' block, then reverted) answers a prompt at its result with a live subagent, then runs a task-notification cycle that calls TodoWrite, for a v1 client with settleAtResult and neutral async tasks, with and without `plan: {}`. Both answer end_turn before any plan update. With the plan capability, the out-of-turn cycle sends one plan_update {planId: "plan", type: "items"}; without it, the legacy plan. In both cases the update comes inside the cycle's async task (between async_task_spawned and async_task_state_update), so the patch's out-of-turn path carries the new plan operation unchanged. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes. The scoped run passes 7 tests in acp-agent.test.ts. The patch's src diff does not reverse-apply because the fork-point patch adds its advertisement next to the settleAtResult one, so the core change was disabled in place by removing the settleAtResult term from endsTurnsWithLiveSubagents. With it disabled, six of the seven scoped tests fail: 'answers the prompt at its result while a subagent is live, for a client that opts into settleAtResult', 'keeps the streamed tool input of a running subagent when the turn ends at its result', 'answers a steer folded into an autonomous cycle at that cycle's result while a subagent is live', 'settles an out-of-turn SandboxNetworkAccess tool call while a subagent is live', 'cancels an out-of-turn permission request before session/close responds' and 'asks out of the turn without a clear-context option'. The seventh, 'is not advertised under ACP v2, which keeps the hold', still passes because the advertisement code was left in place.
tests: npm exec -- vitest run src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts -t settleAtResult

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.102.0 still offers the plan file only to AIR (planFile), and still links an approved plan to its review only for AIR, so the client-neutral form is not absorbed. The patch replays onto v0.102.0 without conflict, and the replayed commit be121ca has the ledger's stable patch-id (69a57ebc). src/exit-plan.ts, src/tool-calls/*, and docs/air-extensions.md are unchanged upstream; the patch's src/acp-agent.ts lines (the linksPlanToReview host callback, the initialize advertisement, and the approvedPlanUpdate in toAcpNotifications) are unchanged. #1554 adds src/plans.ts and a new call site in the /clear reset, resetPlanUpdates(this.clientCapabilities?.plan != null, this.toolCallCapabilities.air.client), which for a plan-capable non-AIR client also sends plan_removed {planId: "plan-mode"}. Upstream exempts AIR because its approved plans are joined to their approval cards. A throwaway probe in acp-agent.test.ts (an approved ExitPlanMode, then /clear) recorded the plan operations per client: a plain v1 client with plan: {} gets plan_update 'plan' (items), plan_update 'plan-mode' (markdown), then plan_removed 'plan' and 'plan-mode'; AIR with plan gets plan_update 'plan-mode:toolu_plan', then only plan_removed 'plan'; the neutral client (plan: {} plus _meta.planFile {version: 1}) gets _meta.planFile.planId and plan_update both as 'plan-mode:toolu_plan', then plan_removed 'plan' and plan_removed 'plan-mode'. A second probe copied the clear-context restart test ('shows a plan approved with clearing the context as the session's markdown plan') for the neutral and AIR clients; both get plan_update 'plan-mode:tool-plan'. The neutral client never receives the unlinked 'plan-mode' ID (live result, replay and clear-context restart all use linksPlanToReview, and v2 ignores the opt-in), so the extra removal targets nothing. In Alas, plan_removed hides only documents whose planId equals the removed ID and bumps planRevisions for that exact ID, while a neutral plan review binds to the payload's 'plan-mode:<id>', so the message is a no-op there. Upstream's PR also accepts sending that removal when no plan was published. The patch's contract (the approved plan has the review's ID 'as for AIR'; the docs say nothing about /clear) still holds, so I retain it unchanged. Strict AIR parity would pass linksPlanToReview at the new reset call site; that change is noted as a doubt and not made. The core change was disabled in place (ClientCapabilities.from forcing neutralPlanFile false). The scoped run then fails 14 of 42 tests, including 'adds the plan file to the tool call and the permission request, and keeps the plan text', 'links a replayed plan to its review', 'links the plan of a client-neutral planFile client by ID' and 'takes the neutral plan file over the AIR planFile'. The clear-context-coordinator case stays green under that red proof because it injects linksPlanToReview directly. Baseline: 42 passed (tool-call-contract 26, acp-scenarios 10, tools 4, acp-v2 1, clear-context-coordinator 1). Probes were reverted and git status --porcelain is empty.

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.102.0 still has only the AIR form of the recommended model (_meta.jetbrains.air.recommendedValue) and no client-neutral recommendedConfigValue key, so the patch is not absorbed. It replays onto v0.102.0 without conflict as 627f3c7, with the ledger's stable patch-id (28697d8a, the same as identity commit 6fdbdcc). The only upstream edits on its paths come from #1557 (SDK 0.3.321, CLI 2.1.321, where Fable 5.2 becomes `fable`): the aliasResumedModelRow doc comment in src/session-model.ts, the resume comment in createSession, and the model-resolution.test.ts fixture. aliasResumedModelRow's code, buildModelConfigOption and the createSession call order (alias, then allowlist, then modelInfos) are unchanged, and ModelInfo in sdk.d.ts is identical between 0.3.319 and 0.3.321. I wrote a throwaway probe in src/tests/acp-agent-settings.test.ts (not committed). It creates a v1 client with the neutral opt-in, resumes a transcript, and lists rows as CLI 2.1.321 does. Results: (1) Resumed Fable 5.2, default resolving to claude-fable-5-2: rows default, fable, claude-fable-5-1, claude-fable-5; currentValue 'default'; record {version: 1, value: 'fable'}. (2) Resumed Fable 5.2, default resolving to claude-opus-5-5 with no opus row: same rows, currentValue 'fable', no record, because the record only names a concrete row that matches the default's resolvedModel. (3) Resumed Fable 5.1 where the CLI lists 5.2 by id: the row stays claude-fable-5-1 because a newer Fable is listed, and the record names 'claude-fable-5-1'. (4) Resumed Fable 5.1 with a `fable` -> 5.2 row: the record names 'claude-fable-5-1' when the default resolves to 5.1. It names 'fable' when the default resolves to 5.2, and then currentValue is 'claude-fable-5-1'. In every case the recorded value is one of the offered option values, and there is no jetbrains key. With aliasResumedModelRow bypassed, cases 1 and 2 and upstream's 'offers Fable 5.1 as `fable` when the CLI resumed on it' fail, because the row and the record go back to claude-fable-5-2. So the neutral record follows upstream's row naming. Upstream's acp-agent-settings Fable test and the updated aliasResumedModelRow unit tests pass on the candidate (13 passed together with the probe). Red proof, in place with exact single matches: the opt-in is forced false and the buildModelConfigOption neutralMeta gate is forced false. Four tests fail: 'client-neutral recommendedConfigValue advert > advertises version 1 to a client that opts in with any version, with no AIR key', 'client-neutral recommendation > names the row of the running default and leaves current default and the rows alone', '... leaves current haiku and the rows alone' and 'sends both records to a client that declares AIR too'. resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.102.0 still publishes the predicted follow-up prompt only to AIR, asks the SDK for promptSuggestions for every client, and has no per-prompt request id, so the patch is still needed. It no longer replays cleanly. The ledger commit is 6f95b38, and its v0.101.1 replay is bc39ecc, both with patch-id 2e2ea943. git merge-tree of bc39ecc onto 0ef5f65 (the exploration candidate without this patch) gives exactly one conflict: the src/acp-agent.ts import block. Upstream #1554 inserted `import { checklistPlanUpdate, resetPlanUpdates } from "./plans.js";` directly above the `./prompt-suggestions.js` import that the patch widens to also import PROMPT_SUGGESTIONS_META_KEY. The adaptation fcdcd00 keeps both imports and touches the same 8 files as 6f95b38. Its added and removed lines (228 +/- lines) are byte-identical to bc39ecc's. Only the context changes (plans.js above, no toGoalSnapshot line), which gives a new stable patch-id, b25bc860. That id is distinct from the retired 2e2ea943 and from 516df919 (d2ddd27). The merge-tree result differs from fcdcd00 only by the conflict markers. No other upstream edit touches publishPromptSuggestion, the prompt-time clear and request-id capture, the prompt_suggestion or result cases, src/prompt-suggestions.ts or the promptSuggestions query option. Claude Agent SDK 0.3.321 changes sdk.d.ts only in doc comments, so the prompt_suggestion message and the promptSuggestions option are unchanged, and tsc passes. #1554 rewrote the conversation_reset branch: publishTaskPlan was replaced by forgetPublishedTaskPlan plus a resetPlanUpdates loop. That loop runs before the patch's untouched `publishPromptSuggestion(params.sessionId, null)` and does not read or reset promptSuggestionExpected, promptSuggestionRequestId or lastPublishedPromptSuggestion. A throwaway probe (src/tests/probe-psr.test.ts, deleted afterwards) used an Alas-like v1 client with plan: {} and the neutral promptSuggestions opt-in. Three cases passed. (a) Prompts turn-1, /clear (turn-2) and turn-3 gave: the prediction with id turn-1; the prompt-time clear {suggestions: []}; plan_removed 'plan' and plan_removed 'plan-mode', with no duplicate clear from the reset because nothing was held; then the turn-3 prediction with its id. (b) A reset after a published prediction sent both plan_removed updates and then {suggestions: []} without an id. (c) A reset between the result and the prediction sent the plan removals and dropped the late prediction. With the patch's src diff reverse-applied, (a) and (b) fail. (c) passes either way by construction. Scoped tests: 27 passed in 4 files. Red proof: `git show fcdcd00 -- src ':!src/tests' | git apply -R` applies cleanly on the candidate. Six tests fail: 'client-neutral: a prompt that asks gets its prediction with its id', 'client-neutral: a turn that predicts only whitespace answers its request with an empty list', 'client-neutral: the same text again still answers the next request', 'client-neutral: a client with both forms gets one update that carries the id', 'asks the SDK for a predicted follow-up prompt per turn only for a client that reads it: any other' and 'client-neutral promptSuggestions advert > advertises version 1 to a client that opts in with any version, with no AIR key'. That is the same set as the v0.101.1 proof. The tree was restored and git status is clean.
